guard: the docs bundle is a build artifact: the built module serves every page in docs/, and the generator refuses a hollow source rather than emitting one
why: WHAT MOVED, AND WHY THE OLD PROOF NO LONGER COVERS IT. The bundle used to be generated and
COMMITTED, and `check:docsbundle` ended in `git diff --exit-code` on it. That diff was the
thing standing between a broken generator and a shipped connector: a human saw the artifact
change in review, and CI saw the tree disagree with the sources.
It was also a conflict generator. Two branches that regenerated the same region of that file
conflicted in it while their source pages merged cleanly -- measured with `git merge-tree
--write-tree`: two edits 260 lines apart in one page, and two branches each ADDING a different
new page, both exit 1 with CONFLICT on the artifact and no conflict in any source. 878 commits
to a file no human wrote.
So the generator now runs from this package's own `build` and `typecheck`, and the path is
gitignored. There is no tracked artifact left to diff, which means THE DIFF THAT USED TO CATCH
A BROKEN GENERATOR IS GONE, and the two cells these mutations grade are what replaced it.
CELL 6 grades coverage: the BUILT module serves every page in `docs/`. The expectation is read
off the filesystem rather than pinned to a count, so adding a page does not redden it -- the
claim is that no page silently stops being served, which is precisely what a generator that
drops entries would do while every other cell in the suite stayed green. Cells 1-5 all read a
handful of named pages, so none of them can see a corpus that quietly shrank.
CELL 7 grades the fail-loud property the generator's own header documents, and it matters more
now than it did when the artifact was committed: the generator runs unattended inside every
build, so its refusal is the only check between an empty page and a release whose `cotal_docs`
answers nothing. It is driven through the REAL generator against a COPY of the sources, so the
repository's docs are never modified and `--out` keeps the connector's artifact untouched.
SPECIFIER BOUNDARY, inherited from this suite's other config and true here for the same reason.
`docs.smoke.ts` imports `@cotal-ai/connector-core`, which resolves to `dist`. A mutation in
`src` under a bare `tsx` command would be VOID ON ARRIVAL. The command therefore carries the
package build -- and because that build now also RUNS THE GENERATOR, a mutation to the
generator reaches `dist` through the same step. `afterRestore` rebuilds, so the tree is not
left holding a `dist` compiled from the mutant; `dist` is gitignored and git cannot recover it.
MARKER IS UPSTREAM ON PURPOSE. Section 5's mark is the last one printed before the region under
test, so reaching it proves the run really got as far as cells 6 and 7 rather than dying early
somewhere harmless. Naming 6's or 7's own mark would make every genuine kill look INCONCLUSIVE,
since a killed run stops before the mark it would have printed.
NOT GRADED, and named rather than implied: the `--out` flag's valueless-argument refusal. It is
a caller-mistake guard on a script argument, and the only realistic mutation (accepting an
undefined path) makes the generator write to the default location -- which is what it did
before the flag existed, so the suite cannot distinguish it from correct behaviour. The check
exists so a mistyped invocation cannot silently overwrite the connector's artifact; it is not a
property this suite can observe.

mutations.name: the generator drops the last page, so a real doc silently stops being served
mutations.expectRed: the built docs module serves every page in docs/
mutations.cell: the built docs module serves every page in docs/
mutations.note: The failure the removed `git diff` used to make visible. A generator that emits 39 of 40 pages produces a bundle that parses, builds, typechecks and serves every page cells 1-5 name -- `cotal_docs` simply answers "no such page" for one real doc. This is aimed at the coverage cell alone: nothing else in the suite counts the corpus.

mutations.name: an empty source page is emitted instead of refused, so a release can ship hollow docs
mutations.find: if (!body.trim()) throw new Error(`gen:docsbundle: docs/${f} is empty`);
mutations.replace: if (false) throw new Error(`gen:docsbundle: docs/${f} is empty`);
mutations.expectRed: an empty source page makes the generator throw rather than emit hollow docs
mutations.cell: an empty source page makes the generator throw rather than emit hollow docs
mutations.note: The fail-loud property the generator's header promises, and the one the build now depends on. With the guard removed the generator succeeds on an empty page and emits an entry with an empty body, which is the hollow-docs release the check exists to prevent.

mutations.name: an empty normative source is not refused, so the bundle ships with no spec
mutations.find: if (!specBody.trim()) throw new Error("gen:docsbundle: SPEC.md is empty");
mutations.replace: if (false) throw new Error("gen:docsbundle: SPEC.md is empty");
mutations.expectRed: an empty normative source makes the generator throw
mutations.cell: an empty normative source makes the generator throw
mutations.note: The other half of cell 7, and a genuinely different failure from the one above: a hollow SPEC.md is not an empty page, and a generator guarding only page emptiness would still ship a bundle whose normative source is empty. Paired with the empty-page mutation so neither leg can carry the cell alone.
